observations: A large dark-green massed shape occupies the center, outlined and overlaid by dense crossing lines in red, white, yellow, teal, and black running in competing directions across the whole surface.
Two small circular forms with concentric rings appear near the upper center of the dark mass, and a jagged pale-yellow wedge shape sits in the upper right corner against a darker ground.
A thin white rectangle frames most of the composition inside the image edge, and the artist's signature appears in white at the lower right, partially overlapping that frame line.
reading: The dark central mass anchors the image while layers of short crossing lines in five or six colors pull outward from it in every direction, creating a sense of pressure rather than stillness. The two ringed circles read as watchful openings in an otherwise dense surface. Warm yellows and oranges at the edges offer some relief against the heavy center.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #22 and nnxyz nnotb #24. Where #22 uses a cool blue-dominant field with open white line structures, #23 presses a dark warm mass into the center, and #24 shifts to a stark red-and-black palette with simplified forms.

connections.reason: Both works use dense overlapping line networks across a large central mass, but #22 keeps its field open and cool-blue while #23 compresses the same approach into a darker, warmer, more congested center.
Both #23 and #24 place two circular eye-like forms near the top of a dominant central shape, but #24 isolates them on a flat red ground while #23 buries them in layered crossing lines.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye find a gap or pause in the line density, and what is visible there?
ambiguities: The jagged pale-yellow wedge in the upper right is unclear in subject — it may be a geometric form or a fragment of a larger shape cropped by the frame.
Title order and recorded creation order align for this work in the owned subset, but gaps exist elsewhere in the nnotb family, so adjacency here is not confirmed as a making sequence.
